data.name: PlayUSA
data.detailed_description:
PlayUSA is an online turn-based strategy game in which the goal is to buy as many cities as you can with your starting balance of $100 billion. To win the game you need to
gain as many points as you can before everybody is out. You can do this by buying cities or buying planes and flying them in between the cities that you own. You can play
with as little as 1 other friend or with up to 3 people from around the globe.



Main Features:

  • Play online around the globe with anyone you desire.
  • Steam Achievements.
  • No port-forwarding required to play anywhere around the world!
  • Explore the USA, buying cities and building a national empire.
  • Controller Support!

Start by strategically bidding your money to start the game, whoever bids highest, wins! Then work through the cities building your empire of planes and networks of cities
and play until you go bust - it is as simple as that!

reviews.review:
PlayUSA is a simple online turn-based strategy game where the goal is to build your own network across the United States. You start with a huge amount of money, buy cities, connect them with planes, and try to earn more points than your opponents before everyone runs out of money. The idea is basically a mix between a board game and a business strategy game.

The main idea behind PlayUSA is actually pretty interesting. Buying cities and creating flight networks gives the game a different feeling compared to normal strategy games. The bidding system at the start also adds some tension because choosing how much money to spend early can affect the rest of the match.

The best part of the game is playing with other people. The strategy becomes more interesting when you are competing against real players because you have to think about where they might expand and whether it is worth spending money to block their plans. With friends, the simple mechanics could create some fun moments.

However, the biggest problem is that the game feels very limited. There are not many systems to learn, and after a few matches you have probably seen most of what it offers. The strategy is there, but it is not very deep compared to bigger board game or management-style games.

The player base is also a problem. Since this is an older small online game, finding active opponents may be difficult. A multiplayer strategy game depends heavily on having people available to play, and without that, a lot of the appeal disappears.

The presentation is also fairly basic. The map idea works, but the game does not have the polish or visual quality of larger strategy games. It feels more like a small digital board game than a full strategy experience.

Overall, PlayUSA is a decent idea that could be fun with the right group of players. The city buying and airline network mechanics are interesting, but the lack of depth and possible player availability issues hold it back. It is worth trying if you have friends who want to play, but it is not a strategy game that will keep most people interested for a long time.

Rating: 6/10
